subject: Hosted API: p50/p95 measurement boundaries, evidence, and temporary onboarding carveout
messages:
From: Natalie Ruiz <natalie.ruiz@datacorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataCorp Contracts <contracts@datacorp.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying p50/p95 evidence and request for onboarding carveout

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the hosted API performance looked promising. Before we sign the SO, our contracts team needs clarity on two items related to the latency SLOs (p50 / p95):

1) Measurement windows & aggregation: our legal team wants to understand exactly how Redwood calculates p50/p95 for the Hosted API. Is this a rolling 24h percentile? Is there any daypart weighting or bucketing applied? We need a short, plain-language description we can include in the Exhibit.

2) Evidence package: what artifacts will Redwood provide each month to demonstrate compliance (e.g., histograms, raw sample traces, canary logs, aggregated per-region percentiles)? We need something that our SREs can consume when validating.

Finally — related to onboarding — we will run a high-throughput ingestion test during the first two weeks that will likely inflate p95 temporarily while we optimize prompts and batching. Is Redwood able to offer a temporary onboarding carveout (no SLA penalties) for that initial ramp if we provide a mutual action plan and accept limited burst protections? If so, what does that look like in terms of duration and evidence required?

Can you send a short reply with the measurement definition and a proposal for the carveout conditions? Contracts would like to close by the end of next week.

Thanks,
Natalie Ruiz
Head of Platform Operations
DataCorp

Attachments: none referenced in this message
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Ruiz <natalie.ruiz@datacorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, DataCorp Contracts <contracts@datacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying p50/p95 evidence and request for onboarding carveout

Hi Natalie —

Appreciate the clear asks. Below is the short, contract-ready wording for how we measure p50/p95 for Hosted API, followed by what we can supply as evidence and a draft onboarding carveout offer. If that looks OK, we can drop this into the Exhibit and Ben will attach the mutual action plan.

Measurement definition (plain language for contract):
- We compute client-facing latency percentiles (p50 and p95) from the set of completed request end-to-end latencies observed by the serving fleet for that customer in the specified region.
- Aggregation period: rolling 12-hour measurement window sampled on the hour to produce hourly percentiles. Reported daily values are the median of the 12 most recent hourly samples. This reduces sensitivity to single-minute spikes while preserving responsiveness to degradations.
- Regional treatment: percentiles are computed per AWS region (or equivalent cloud region). A regional SLO breach is determined by the region's reported p95 exceeding the contractual threshold for two consecutive daily values.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows (pre-notified) and verified third-party infra incidents are excluded; we capture exclusion records in the evidence package.

Evidence package (monthly):
- Per-region percentile CSV (hourly samples for the month)
- Aggregated histogram images (PNG) and the underlying bucket counts (CSV)
- 50 random trace samples from canaries during any alleged breach window (zip of traces)
- Event notes describing any exclusions and the rationale (markdown)

Onboarding carveout proposal (customer-friendly):
- One 30-day onboarding grace period, triggered by customer request and mutual action plan (MAP). The grace period will: 
  * Exempt the customer from SLA penalties for p95 exceedances observed during the 30-day window.
  * Require the customer to run with the documented burst profile (max QPS and concurrency limits) and accept Redwood's burst protection throttles to protect co-tenants.
  * Require Redwood and DataCorp to exchange 3 interim evidence snapshots (day 7, day 15, day 30) showing hourly percentile CSVs and a short remediation plan if p95 remains above target.

If you accept the above, we will:
- Attach the MAP (I drafted a template) and the monthly evidence manifest to the Exhibit.
- Provide a zipped evidence bundle (redwood_latency_evidence_v2.zip) after each interim snapshot and for the month close.

I attached a sample measurement histogram and the MAP draft to illustrate. Let me know whether DataCorp wants a 30-day or 14-day grace window and whether we should start it on the contract effective date or a separate onboarding start date.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: redwood_latency_evidence_v2.zip (sample CSVs + traces), measurement_histogram.png, DC-4873-MAP.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Ruiz <natalie.ruiz@datacorp.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, DataCorp Contracts <contracts@datacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying p50/p95 evidence and request for onboarding carveout

Adding a quick, operational note from the Dedicated/Hosted ops side:

We can support the 30-day onboarding grace period with the following guardrails:
- Redwood will enable per-customer burst protection and throttling for the onboarding window; sustained bursts above the agreed profile will trigger requests to your SRE to throttle back.
- We require DataCorp to pin a dedicated model variant for the onboarding window (to remove model-change noise) or accept a documented fallback policy.
- During the grace period, we will still collect and share all evidence — the difference is there is no financial penalty tied to p95 for that 30 days.

If DataCorp needs the 14-day version instead, we can do that too; choice affects the number of interim snapshots (two for 14-day, three for 30-day).

Ben Carter
Sr. PM, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

(We will produce the MAP.xlsx with the scheduling milestones and sign-off columns once Natalie confirms the window.)
From: Natalie Ruiz <natalie.ruiz@datacorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataCorp Contracts <contracts@datacorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying p50/p95 evidence and request for onboarding carveout

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed.

We accept the 30-day onboarding grace period. A couple of quick asks before we finalize:
- Please add the exact rolling-window wording you sent into Exhibit B (so it's contractual language).
- For the MAP, we will start the onboarding window on 2027-06-23 (two business days after signature) and will provide our initial burst profile by EOD 2027-06-24.
- DataCorp requests that Redwood include the HubSpot deal id (DC-4873) and a DocuSign envelope for the Exhibit addendum.

Contracts will prepare the redlines for the main agreement; please attach the MAP and the evidence manifest to the HubSpot deal and share a DocuSign link when ready. Once we have the docusign we will sign and trigger the 30-day period on 2027-06-23.

Appreciate the speedy turnaround.

—Natalie
Head of Platform Operations, DataCorp

Attachments: none
